family_lesson.where_to_look_first: Start with a woody plant with alternate simple entire leaves, often with latex, then inspect the axillary flower clusters. Sapotaceae flowers are small and regular with a fused corolla; in Sideroxylon the fertile stamens stand opposite the corolla lobes and alternate with petaloid staminodes. Confirm with a superior multi-loculed ovary and a fleshy berry containing a hard glossy seed.
family_lesson.strongest_field_confirmation: Woody habit + sticky/milky latex when naturally exposed + alternate entire leaves + small axillary fascicles + sympetalous radial flowers with stamens opposite corolla lobes and alternating staminodes + fleshy berry + hard shiny seed.
core_characters: Latex nearly always present in bark, twigs, petioles and/or fruit; often white and sticky.
Leaves simple, usually alternate/spiral and entire; stipules absent or short-lived.
Flowers bisexual and radial in the local Sideroxylon anchor.
Corolla fused; in Sideroxylon each corolla lobe may carry lateral appendages.
Fertile stamens are opposite the corolla lobes.
Petaloid staminodes alternate with the fertile stamens.
Ovary superior and multi-loculed, with one ovule per locule.
Seeds are hard, often shiny, with a conspicuous hilum/scar.
avoid_overgeneralizing: Do not make thorns mandatory: Sideroxylon lanuginosum can be armed or unarmed.
Do not injure trees solely to test latex; use already-broken twigs, fruit, or minimal diagnostic damage only when appropriate.
Do not confuse the family with Ebenaceae based on black fruit alone.
Do not assume local Sideroxylon fruit contains several seeds; S. lanuginosum commonly matures a single large seed.
Do not force a subspecies ID for local S. lanuginosum until the conflicting albicans/oblongifolium treatments are reconciled.

anchor_card.status: Priority 1; Hays Local + NPSOT + Personal List; 17 wild observations; species curation pending
anchor_card.taxonomy: Current POWO and FNA accept Sideroxylon lanuginosum with three accepted subspecies.
anchor_card.look_here_first: Look for a semi-evergreen/deciduous woody plant with alternate entire leaves, woolly or hairy leaf undersides, short spur shoots that may end in sharp spines, small pale axillary flower clusters, and black berries.
confirms: Branches may be thorn-tipped/spinescent, but armature is variable.
Leaf underside commonly villous/tomentose or woolly, often much paler than the upper surface.
Small axillary fascicles of numerous flowers.
Five sepals and usually five pale cream/white/yellowish corolla lobes.
Five fertile stamens opposite the corolla lobes.
Five petaloid staminodes alternating with the fertile stamens.
Superior 5(-8)-loculed ovary, each locule with one ovule.
Purplish-black to black berry about 7–12 mm in FNA.
Usually one hard large glossy seed in the local Williamson treatment.

flower_lesson.key_point: Sideroxylon is excellent for teaching staminodes because the flower alternates five fertile stamens with five petaloid sterile staminodes.
sequence: label fertile stamen opposite that lobe
label petaloid staminode between adjacent stamens
flower_lesson.memory_line: stamen opposite petal lobe; staminode in between

latex_lesson.key_point: Sticky white latex is a powerful Sapotaceae clue, but it should be treated as supporting evidence rather than an excuse to damage the plant.
latex_lesson.field_rule: Prefer naturally broken tissue, fallen fruit, an already-cut twig, or an incidental scratch. Do not routinely cut healthy woody plants just to prove the family.
latex_lesson.comparison_value: Latex is particularly useful against Diospyros and Ilex, which can overlap in leaf and fruit appearance but do not use the same classic Sapotaceae latex cue.

thorn_lesson.key_point: Short shoots/stems may terminate in sharp spines in Sideroxylon lanuginosum.
thorn_lesson.caution: FNA explicitly describes stems as armed or unarmed, so a thorn is strong supporting evidence when present but its absence does not rule the species out.

fruit_seed_lesson.key_point: The local gum-bumelia fruit is a small black berry surrounding a disproportionately large, hard, glossy seed.
fruit_seed_lesson.local_detail: Williamson material is described as a roughly 10 mm black berry with a glossy black seed around 7–9 mm long.
fruit_seed_lesson.family_value: The hard shiny seed with a conspicuous scar is a useful Sapotaceae trait and separates the fruit anatomy from Ilex pyrenes and Diospyros multi-seeded berries.

infraspecific_taxonomy_hold.issue: Local-source names are not fully concordant.
infraspecific_taxonomy_hold.Hays_source: UT Hays flora lists Sideroxylon lanuginosum subsp. albicans.
infraspecific_taxonomy_hold.Williamson_source: UT Williamson treatment uses Sideroxylon lanuginosum subsp. oblongifolium.
infraspecific_taxonomy_hold.POWO: POWO treats Sideroxylon lanuginosum subsp. albicans as a synonym of subsp. lanuginosum.
infraspecific_taxonomy_hold.FNA: FNA lists the old albicans name in synonymy under subsp. oblongifolium and recognizes oblongifolium by white/gray abaxial hairs.
infraspecific_taxonomy_hold.learner_rule: Do not resolve individual Central Texas plants below species in the first learner module. Teach Sideroxylon lanuginosum first and flag subspecies as a dedicated later review.

fast_key: Woody shrub/tree + alternate entire leaves + sticky/milky latex -> strongly consider Sapotaceae.
Axillary tiny pale flower fascicles + 5 fertile stamens alternating with 5 petaloid staminodes -> Sideroxylon/Sapotaceae strongly supported.
Hairy/woolly lower leaf surface + black berry + possible thorn-tipped shoots -> Sideroxylon lanuginosum framework.
Black berry with one large hard glossy seed -> supports local gum bumelia.
Large persistent calyx beneath berry + no latex cue -> reconsider Diospyros/Ebenaceae.
Small drupe with several hard pyrenes + interpetiolar/holly architecture -> reconsider Ilex/Aquifoliaceae.

Ebenaceae.confusion: Alternate entire leaves, small pale flowers and dark fleshy fruit overlap.
Ebenaceae.tie_breaker: Diospyros has a conspicuous persistent/accrescent calyx under the fruit and lacks the classic sticky milky Sapotaceae latex; local Sideroxylon fruit typically has one large glossy seed.

Aquifoliaceae.confusion: Woody plants with alternate leaves and small axillary flowers/fruits.
Aquifoliaceae.tie_breaker: Ilex fruit is a drupe with several hard pyrenes and plants lack the Sapotaceae latex/staminode pattern; Sideroxylon has sympetalous flowers with stamens opposite corolla lobes and alternating staminodes.

Rhamnaceae.confusion: Thorny woody shrubs with small flowers and dark drupaceous fruit.
Rhamnaceae.tie_breaker: Rhamnaceae often has stipules and characteristic venation and lacks sticky milky Sapotaceae latex; Sapotaceae Sideroxylon flowers also show opposite stamens + alternating petaloid staminodes.
